repo.description:
## Impact

The expression sandbox did not rewrite free identifiers appearing in spread, computed-key, switch-case, or class-extension positions, so they resolved against the process globals, leaving over thirty host globals reachable from a workflow expression. Any authenticated user with workflow-edit permission could mutate those shared objects, and the change persisted process-wide across all later expression evaluations until restart.

## Patches

The issue has been fixed in n8n versions 2.35.4 and 2.36.2. Users should upgrade to one of these versions or later to remediate the vulnerability.

## Workarounds

If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should consider the following temporary mitigations:
- Restrict n8n instance access to fully trusted users only.
- On self-hosted deployments, restart the n8n process periodically to clear any accumulated mutations.

These workarounds do not fully remediate the risk and should only be used as short-term mitigation measures.
repo.summary: Expression Sandbox SpreadElement Bypass Enables Persistent Cross-Evaluation Native Object Mutation
